extension_policies: extras, tool arguments, provider option values and route results are open JSON owned by their provider, tool or plugin; the manifest describes their policy rather than their shape
unknown fields are ignored unless a record declares rejection
remote-tool routes are an open registry: the connection path names the route and no body field overrides it
an unrecognized event name is not an envelope failure; a hub must tolerate future events
the manifest describes built-in shapes only; it is not a claim that a configured provider or plugin capability is enabled
fingerprint_scope: certified: field names, kinds, presence, nullability, closed vocabularies, record references, the event registry and the message registry

not certified: ordering and delivery guarantees, backpressure and admission policy, cancellation and shutdown behaviour, confirmation deadlines, authorization and security judgement, persistence atomicity, and every explanatory sentence

AnswerPage.description: Exact answer bytes with the cursor to continue; binary parts are unavailable.

AnswerSource.description: Locator for exact-answer pagination. Every field must be copied unchanged.

ArchiveCleanup.description: Archives removed after a successful compaction.

ArchiveRef.description: Storage evidence of a compaction archive; never an answer-paging source.

AutoCompact.description: Attempt/success counters for the current request plus the startup policy; a zero threshold disables it.

Call.description: A proposed tool call. Arguments are tool-owned; the classifications are not.

CompactFinishedData.description: Compacted state was durably published; old history pages must be invalidated.

ConfirmationOptions.description: Per-run confirmation policy; only mode is remotely configurable.

ConfirmationRequest.description: One confirmation request. Correlate by all four identifiers plus the authenticated connection; there is no request ID or event sequence.

ConfirmationRequestEnvelope.description: Worker-to-hub confirmation request on its own connection.

ConfirmationResponse.description: One decision for one request. A mismatched identifier denies the call.

ConfirmationResponseEnvelope.description: Hub-to-worker decision, sent once on the same confirmation connection.

Content.description: One ordered content part. Display projections may add truncation markers; canonical execution bytes never carry them.

EmptyData.description: An empty object. Older workers may omit fields; nothing is required.

ErrorData.description: Control-validation or storage diagnostic, not a universal fatal notification. A terminal storage failure always carries primary_outcome.

EventEnvelope.description: An emitted event. data carries the shape registered for this event name.

EventQueue.description: Queue and transport byte snapshot; a snapshot is not a delivery receipt.

ExecutionIdentity.description: Worker, request and run identity of an input or a committed response.

ExportErrorData.description: Optional archive-cleanup diagnostic; it never changes the run outcome.

FailureData.description: Where a run failed and whether an explicit continue may be admitted.

HistoryPage.description: One history page. All pages of a load must agree on worker, revision and total.

HistoryStep.description: One bounded response preview. Exact text is read through answer pages.

HistoryTurn.description: One canonical turn with a repeated user projection; steps are admitted whole.

InputAdmittedData.description: Admitted operation retained for transcript replay; older workers emitted an empty object.

InputRejectedData.description: An input that failed validation or queue admission; no run was started for it.

LoopProgress.description: Current or most recent loop outcome and recovery boundary, unrelated to event sequence.

MemoryRetention.description: Effective archive retention; zero disables cleanup.

OmissionMarker.description: Counts a batch suffix that was not projected; it is not a call or a result.

OmissionSummary.description: An explicit omission instead of an apparently complete summary prefix.

OptionCategory.description: Advertised choices and effective current values; an absent key means no selection.

OptionChoice.description: An option name with its advertised values, in display order.

Options.description: Optional payload categories applied at the next run boundary; unknown categories are rejected.

OptionsData.description: Available choices and current selections grouped by category.

PayloadRequest.description: A message, continuation, compaction, history query or answer query; the operation decides which fields are required.

PersistedData.description: A required snapshot write completed at the named boundary; notifications may be coalesced.

PlanReadArguments.description: Arguments of plan/read: the operation is the literal read.

PlanReadResult.description: Current plan text, its revision and timestamp; the initial plan is revision 0 with null time.

PlanReplaceArguments.description: Arguments of plan/replace: replace plus at most 64 KiB of markdown.

PlanReplaceResult.description: Outcome of a replacement: unchanged content does not increment the revision.

QueryErrorData.description: Query failure. request_id echoes whatever the query carried, including null.

RequestContent.description: One admitted user part. raw must be nonempty and extras, when present, an object.

ResponseProjection.description: A committed response as displayed: bounded content with its cursor fields. Exact text is read through answer pages.

Result.description: A tool result. Recognized extras markers include error, cause_query and loop_skipped.

RunOutcomeData.description: Settled invocation outcome. Omission counters appear only when nonzero and are not lifetime totals or delivery acknowledgements.

SignalEnvelope.description: Hub-to-worker signal envelope; it uses a separate queue from payloads.

SignalRequest.description: Control signal; additional fields are ignored and no request ID is echoed.

StatusData.description: State snapshot. Optional fields are omitted by older workers and must be tolerated.

ToolError.description: Machine-readable rejection code with a diagnostic message.

ToolRequest.description: One remote-tool request. Routes are an open registry; the first segment names the family.

ToolRequestEnvelope.description: One-shot remote-tool request; the route is the connection path.

ToolResponse.description: Echoes the identifiers and route. succeeded carries result, rejected carries error.

ToolResponseEnvelope.description: Terminal remote-tool answer; the connection closes after it.

ToolResultMessage.description: One returned batch entry: the message projection carrying its invoke_return provenance.

Usage.description: Provider-reported token cost; cache_hit counts tokens inside prompt.
